newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Rescuers hear sounds in resort landslide rubble.
newsitem.headline: Rescuers hear sounds in resort landslide rubble.

text.p: Rescue workers, who had almost despaired of finding anyone alive, heard muffled sounds on Saturday under the rubble of two ski lodges destroyed by a landslide, police said.
Twenty people are thought to have been entombed in Wednesday night's landslide in the ski village of Thredbo, in Australia's Snowy Mountains, when a slope gave way, destroying two lodges.
"We've head muffled sounds under the concrete slabs," police spokesman Mark Hargraves told reporters. "They (rescue workers) are going berserk up there trying to move as much rubble as they can".
Police earlier put the confirmed death toll at three, revising it downwards from four. They said one body had been recovered and two others had been located by rescue workers.
Search crews worked in the mangled wreckage all through the night under lights in freezing conditions.
